entities.summary:
Wilhelm von Brandenburg was a Latvian Catholic prelate who served as Archbishop of Riga from 1539 to 1561. Born into a prominent noble family, von Brandenburg's early life was marked by his education at the University of Königsberg, where he studied theology and law. In 1539, he was appointed Archbishop of Riga by the Holy Roman Emperor, Charles V, and played a crucial role in the city's governance and ecclesiastical affairs.

As Archbishop, von Brandenburg oversaw the construction of Riga Cathedral and the establishment of the Riga Seminary, a school for Catholic clergy. He also worked to promote the Protestant Reformation in the region, despite the dominant Catholic influence. Von Brandenburg's efforts to balance the interests of Catholics and Protestants in Riga contributed to the city's relative stability during a time of religious turmoil in Europe.

Von Brandenburg's legacy extends beyond his time in Riga, as he played a key role in the development of the Lutheran Church in Livonia. His successors continued to build upon his work, shaping the religious landscape of the region for centuries to come.

The exact date of von Brandenburg's death is unknown, but it is believed to have occurred in 1563.
